ordering_check.root_cause: Merge re-sorts all candidates by score (= last_date) DESC, article_idx ASC, implementing recency_only ordering for the final output. The production ordering in repurchase.py affects source_rank (which k articles enter the pool), but the merge re-sorting makes the final top-12 identical to what recency_only ordering would produce.
ordering_check.mismatch_explanation: The +0.000196 mismatch reported in earlier sessions was NOT due to the purchase_count tie-break. The true cause was a bug in the old inline EDA reimplementation of Baseline B inside regression_check(), likely in the popularity fill path (different time window or k). Switching to the actual src pipeline (recency_only + generate_global_last_week) fixed the mismatch by correctly replicating EDA Baseline B.
